The other types are full-wipe and inactive. -f forces the command without confirmation. For a simple database wipe use clear database instead.

Just run time. The command displays the system's time and takes no parameters; it is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Output looks like 2020-06-29T22:29:37+00:00. It reports the time based on the system configured timezone. For more detail use show clock, which returns current-time, universal-time, timezone, uptime, uptime-seconds, time-source, DST-active and last-time-jump, although show clock may take up to 2 minutes if the DNS server is not properly configured.

The uptime command displays system uptime and load average, for example: 21:24:09 up 41 days, 15:56, 1 user, load average: 0.10, 0.35, 0.39. The load average, also called average system load, indicates whether there are multiple tasks queued on the system (on the card). Whether it is high or low depends on the number of cores the system has, how many CPUs are integrated into the card, and the number itself. The rule stated in the guide: a load average value is considered to be high when it is greater than the number of CPUs on the card. uptime takes no parameters and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Uptime alone is also available from show clock (uptime, uptime-seconds) and on the status system dashboard.

Yes. The command is manual-switchover [-f] [resource=]<value>, where resource is the AID of the object to be manually switched. It prompts with: Controller will switchover and connection to the management interface will be lost. Do you want to continue? [y/n]. You confirm at that prompt to proceed, or use -f to force it without confirmation. Examples by chassis: manual-switchover card-1-3 on a 1830 GX G42, manual-switchover card-1-5 on a G32, manual-switchover card-1-12 on a G34c. Access mode is Operational mode. For the full procedure see the 1830 GX Software Management Procedures Guide.

show protection. It is a show-only command used to display the node's protection container, it takes no parameters, and its access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For the individual objects inside it, use show protection-group-<name> for group state, timers and requests, and show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name> for the state and role of each member.

On protection-group-<name>, switching-mode takes unidirectional or bidirectional and defaults to unidirectional. The wait-to-restore timer is wtr-timer: the trigger clearance soaking time before reverting to the working protection unit, measured and set in 1-second steps, range 60..720 seconds, default 300 seconds. It is only applicable in revertive mode, and reversion-mode (revertive or non-revertive) defaults to non-revertive, so you must set reversion-mode revertive for the WTR timer to apply. show protection-group-<name> remaining-wtr returns the time left, range 0..720 seconds, again only in revertive mode. The companion timer is hold-off-timer, the switching trigger soaking time before switching, measured and set in 1-millisecond steps, range 0..10000 ms, default 0. These attributes are available on both add and set.

Use the operating command protection-switch [-f] [operation-type=]<value> [switch-target=]<value> [protection-group=]<value>. For a force to the protection path: protection-switch protection-group-test operation-type=force switch-target=protection. operation-type accepts force, lockout, manual and release. switch-target is the target of the switch command and is not needed for the release and lockout operations. -f forces the command without confirmation. Access mode is Operational mode. The same intent can be expressed on the object itself through the pg-request attribute of protection-group-<name>, which takes clear, manual-to-working, manual-to-protection, forced-to-working, forced-to-protection, protection-lockout and exercise (exercise applies only to bidirectional SNCP), with a default of clear.

Use show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name> and read the state attribute, which takes active, standby, available or unknown. The companion attribute role tells you whether that unit is the working or the protection member. The same show also returns AID, transport-entity, alarm-report-control and label. Only alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default inhibited) and label are settable; state and role are show only. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. At the group level, show protection-group-<name> pg-state and last-switch-trigger tell you why the traffic is where it is.

Most alarms have automatic raise and clear criteria, but a very small subset has no clear criteria and must be acknowledged and cleared manually. Clear them with clear [-f] alarm [alarm-type=]<value> [[resource=]<value>[,<value>]*], for example clear alarm DBRESTOREFAIL; -f forces the command without confirmation. To find which alarms qualify, list the inventory entries whose can-be-cleared-by-user is true: show alarm-inventory can-be-cleared-by-user=true. This mechanism applies only to system alarms that are not associated with any particular resource, that is system wide or global alarms. Access mode is Operational mode. Note that acknowledging is a separate action: set-alarm-state [state=]<value> with states none, ack or close, applied to all-alarms or to an alarm-id-list of 1 to 10 alarm ids, with an optional acknowledge-text of up to 256 characters.

That is controlled system wide by set alarm-control arc-behavior <value>. arc-behavior is the system wide alarm-reporting-control switch and takes leave-alarms, which when ARC is set to inhibit leaves current alarms in a raised mode, or clear-alarms, which when ARC is set to inhibit clears the current alarms. The default is leave-alarms, so by default already-raised alarms stay up. Read it back with show alarm-control. The same object also carries alarm-soaking-behavior, values automatic (soaking time as defined in the FM profile) or no-soak (certain alarms specified in the FM profile get no soaking time), default automatic; the OSC LOF alarm uses the per-facility user-configurable lof-soak-timer on the PBAx card. Access mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Alarms suppressed by ARC can still be seen with get-conditions.

Look it up in the alarm inventory, which holds the static information for every possible alarm type in the system: show alarm-inventory-<alarm-type> [resource-type] [alarm-category] [alarm-type-description] [corrective-action] [default-severity] [service-affecting], for example show alarm-inventory-TIM or show alarm-inventory-MSIM. alarm-type-description is a string up to 128 characters explaining the alarm, and corrective-action is system provided information on how to correct the situation that triggered it, up to 256 characters. alarm-category is one of communication, facility, equipment, environmental, processing-error, software, quality-of-service or security. default-severity lists the possible default severities (critical, major, minor, warning, not-reported, event), since the same alarm may default differently per resource-type. service-affecting is indeterminate, sa, nsa or sa-nsa. Access mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Yes. alarm-severity-entry configures the severity for one particular alarm on one particular resource type. Syntax: set alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> [severity <value>]. resource-type is the resource being modified (for example CHM1R, FAN, 1830 GX G31), alarm-type is the abbreviated alarm code (for example ADMIN-LOCK, BERSD), direction is na, ingress or egress, and location is na, near-end or far-end. severity takes critical, event, major, minor, not-reported or warning. Example: set alarm-severity-entry-OTU2/TIM/ingress/near-end severity minor, or set alarm-severity-entry-tom/EQPTCOMFAIL severity major. Read it back with show alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> [severity] [service-affecting], or show alarm-severity-entry for all entries. The object is system managed and cannot be manually deleted. Press ? after the command to list the available entities.

They operate at different granularity. alarm-severity-entry targets one specific alarm on one resource type with the full key: set alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> severity <value>, for example set alarm-severity-entry-OTU2/TIM/ingress/near-end severity minor. alarm-severity-profile sets the severity for an alarm profile instead: set alarm-severity-profile <profile-entry> severity <critical|event|major|minor|not-reported|warning>, for example set alarm-severity-profile alarm-severity-entry-trusted-certificate/CERTIFICATE-EXPIRED severity critical. Both accept the same six severity values and both objects are managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. show alarm-severity-profile takes no parameters and lists the profiles; press ? after set alarm-severity-profile to display the available profiles. Access mode for both is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use show current-alarms, which shows the list of currently raised alarms and carries two attributes: number-of-alarms, a number giving how many alarms are currently raised, and last-changed, a timestamp of the last change in the current alarm list, meaning either a raise or a clear event. You can request them individually, for example show current-alarms number-of-alarms or show current-alarms last-changed. Access mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. For a per-severity breakdown alongside other node data, the status system dashboard prints a line such as 13 current alarms (1 critical, 5 major, 2 not-reported, 5 minor).

Use get-conditions. A condition is an alarm that is not considered current, which happens when the alarm severity is configured as not-reported or not-alarmed, when the alarm is suppressed due to alarm correlation, when it is suppressed due to ARC (alarm reporting control), or when it is suppressed due to AINS. Syntax: get-conditions [[direction=]<value>] [[resource=]<value>] [[resource-type=]<value>] [[alarm-type=]<value>] [[location=]<value>] [[AID=]<value>]. direction takes all, na, ingress or egress and defaults to all; location takes all, na, near-end or far-end and also defaults to all; resource, resource-type, alarm-type and AID are free filters with no default. Access mode is Operational mode. If ARC is the cause, note that alarm-control arc-behavior defaults to leave-alarms.

Use set-alarm-state in Operational Mode: set-alarm-state [state=]<value> [[acknowledge-text=]<value>] (all-alarms | [alarm-id-list=]<value>[,<value>]*). The state parameter is mandatory and takes an operator-state; the selectable values are none, ack and close. Use all-alarms to set all currently raised alarms, or alarm-id-list to name a specific set (from 1 up to 10 alarm ids). acknowledge-text is optional and inserts an acknowledge message stored in the alarm itself, a string of length 0..256. Setting alarms to their current state is accepted, with only the text being updated. Example: set-alarm-state ack all-alarms acknowledge-text=example

Yes. The syntax is clear [-f] statistics [target=]<value>[,<value>]*, in Operational Mode. target is an instance-identifier naming the objects that will have their event counter statistics cleared; -f forces the command without confirmation and -h displays help. Scope is narrow: currently the only supported object type is aaa-server, and AAA statistics are supported for TACACS+ servers but not for RADIUS servers. Clear all AAA servers with clear statistics aaa-server, or a single one with clear statistics aaa-server-MyServer.

Use show [-n=<number>] [-t] log [<logname> [exclude=<exclude-column> ...]]. The -n=x option displays only the last x log entries and -t switches from the default CSV output to an aligned table display, so: show -n=5 -t log security. If the table becomes too wide, remove unwanted columns by adding exclude=<column> after the logname (tab auto-complete lists the removable columns), and you can post-process with piped commands, for example show log security | exclude john | include NETCONF. Valid lognames include messages, linecard, shell-command, netconf-command, apps, cli-command, alarm, configuration, kernel, user, event, security and ztp. Note that due to system restrictions the security log may not be cleared.

Yes, that is expected: console logging is off by default. The log-console enabled attribute takes true or false and defaults to false, so nothing reaches the console until you run set log-console enabled true. The other attribute is source-facilities, the list of syslog facilities used in this configuration: all, authentication, clock-daemon-15, clock-daemon-9, ftp-daemon, kernel, line-printer, local1, local2, local3, local4, local5, local6, local7, log-alert, log-audit, mail-system, network-news, ntp, security, syslog-internal, system-daemons, user-level, uucp. Check the current values with show log-console. Access mode: Operational mode, Candidate Configuration mode.

Add a severity selector with add log-console-facility-filter-<name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>]. The <name> identifies a single syslog facility, or all of them if the value is all. severity takes emergency (level 0), alert (1), critical (2), error (3), warning (4), notice (5), informational (6) or debug (7), and defaults to informational. compare-op specifies how the severity comparison is performed: equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals, defaulting to equals-or-higher. So add log-console-facility-filter-all severity 'critical' filters console log messages down to critical and above. Use set to change it, show to view severity and compare-op, and delete log-console-facility-filter-<name> to remove it.

Retention is set per local file by the log-file command: add log-file-<name> [number-of-files <value>] [max-file-size <value>] [source-facilities <string>] [pattern-match <string>] [sensitive-data <value>]. max-file-size is the maximum file size before rotation in megabytes, uint8 range 1..30, default 30. number-of-files is the maximum number of log files retained, uint8 range 1..20, default 10; when rotating files because max size was reached, the oldest files are discarded if the total number of files is greater than number-of-files. So by default the node keeps up to 10 files of up to 30 MB each. name is a string of 0...128 characters, given without the .log extension. Locally saved files can be emptied with clear or removed with delete, but the default system log file cannot be edited or deleted.

Yes. Restrict the file to the authentication facility (syslog facility 4, authentication/authorization attempt messages), then optionally filter severity. First add log-file-<name> source-facilities authentication (source-facilities defaults to all). Then add log-file-facility-filter-<log-file-name>/<log-file-facility-filter-name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>], where the filter name identifies a single syslog facility or all. severity takes emergency, alert, critical, error, warning, notice, informational or debug and defaults to informational; compare-op takes equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals and defaults to equals-or-higher. For example: add log-file-facility-filter-authlog/authentication severity warning compare-op equals-or-higher. Use set, show and delete on the same key.

Configure the collector with add log-server-<name> address <IP address> ... port <value> ... transport <udp|tls|tcp>, and set transport tls (transport defaults to udp). Unless you say otherwise, port defaults to 514 (range 1..65535) and message-format defaults to rfc5424 (the alternative is rfc3164). Other defaults: enabled true, message-coalescence true, origin manual, source-facilities all, destination-facility-override disabled, sensitive-data none, alarm-report-control allowed. The server name is a string of 0...64 characters and address may be an IPv4 address, IPv6 address or DNS domain name. pattern-match is an optional regular expression, string length 0..255.

Yes, per server: add log-server-facility-filter-<log-server-name>/<log-server-facility-filter-name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>]. The filter name is a facility selector identifying a single syslog facility (kernel, user-level, mail-system, system-daemons, authentication, syslog-internal, line-printer, network-news, uucp, clock-daemon-9, security, ftp-daemon, ntp, log-audit, log-alert, clock-daemon-15, local0..local7) or all. severity takes emergency, alert, critical, error, warning, notice, informational or debug, default informational; compare-op takes equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals, default equals-or-higher. It cannot widen the scope: the filter is based on the source-facilities leaf-list and can only add a filter to the configured source facilities. Example: add log-server-facility-filter-server184/local2 severity debug

Set the global switch: set syslog remote-logging-switch false. That flag disables all remote logging destinations while your configured log-server entries stay in place; its default is true. The syslog container also carries source-address (address or hostname inserted in the HOST field, default localhost), log-file-message-coalescence (true/false, default true), log-relay (remote logging from a shelf controller to a node controller, default false), assignment-method (both, manual or dhcp, default both), niap-compliant-logging (default false), privacy-mode, the GDPR filter (default false), alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default allowed) and label (string 0..256). Verify with show syslog remote-logging-switch. Access mode: Operational mode, Candidate Configuration mode.

The shared-secret attribute of aaa-server is typed String (length 0...128) with the default value sharedkey, but the enforced limit is lower: the maximum length of shared-secret is 64 characters, and any value more than 64 characters is denied with an error message. Set it with add aaa-server-<server-name> ... [shared-secret <value>] or set aaa-server-<server-name> shared-secret <value>; the shared secret is displayed as * when shown. For reference, the server-name itself is a string of length 1...64 and common-password is a string of length 1...128. Access mode: Operational Mode, Candidate Configuration Mode.

That is expected behaviour, not a bug. For TACACS+, the default authentication protocol includes both PAP and CHAP, and the authentication-requests counter tracks each retry and each authentication protocol attempted independently, so authentication requests may increase by 2 for each retry. View the counters with show aaa-statistics-<server-name> [connection-failures] [authentication-requests] [authentication-rejects] [authorization-requests] [authorization-rejects] [accounting-requests]; connection-failures includes failures due to unavailable servers and timeouts. aaa-statistics is only available for AAA servers that use the TACACS+ protocol.

If you omit action, the ACE default action is drop; the permitted values are drop, accept and reject. Limits: sequence-id, which establishes the relative order of the ACE within the ACL, ranges 1-100 for AUX and DCN-B interfaces and 1-256 for the DCN-A interface, and it is recommended to use multiples of 5 so rules can be inserted later. A maximum of 16 ACEs can be created on an ACL if both upper-port and lower-port values are specified; adding a further such ACE when 16 already exist returns an error. Pre-condition: an ACL must be in place before an ACE can be added, and at least one of source IP, destination IP, L4 ports, TTL or protocol must be provided. Other defaults: direction input, protocol any, logging-action false, ttl 255, port bounds 0.

Attach an ACL with add acl-<name> type <value> interface <value> [admin-state <value>]. The interface values are 1-AUX-1, 1-AUX-2, DCN, DCN-B, DCN-2 and DCN-2-B; use add acl-name interface ? to see the available interfaces. Yes, IPv6 is handled: type indicates the top-level type of ACL, that is which fields of the associated IPv4 or IPv6 headers it matches on, and takes IPv4 or IPv6. name is a string of 0...30 characters and admin-state takes lock, maintenance or unlock with default unlock. Example: add acl-AuxV4traffic interface 1-AUX-2 type ipv4. An ACL can be added on the DCN-B interface when the DCN is operating in active-active configuration.

Yes: show access-control-list. It takes no parameters and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For a specific list use show acl-<name> [admin-state] [oper-state] [avail-state] [type] [interface], and for the individual entries within a list use show ace-<name>/<sequence-id> [label] [direction] [logging-action] [source-ip-address] [source-lower-port] [source-upper-port] [destination-ip-address] [destination-lower-port] [destination-upper-port] [ttl] [action] [protocol].

Put a deny rule in an access-rule-list that is bound to the group. First create the list and bind it: add access-rule-list-<name> user-group <group>. Then add the rule: add access-rule-<access-rule-list-name>/<access-rule-name> action <value> [sequence-id <value>] [module-name <value>] [path <value>] [attribute <value>] [attribute-value <value>] [operation <value>] [description <value>]. action is mandatory and takes permit or deny. path is the target object, an XPath of a YANG data node, notification or RPC, or an external command, string max 255 characters, default *. operation is a bits value from create, read, update, delete and execute (default *), and multiple values can be set at once, so write access is create update delete. Example: add access-rule-1/rule path /ne/equipment/card operation create action deny. The system supports a maximum of 500 access-rules across all access-rule-lists.

Order is set by sequence-id: the lists and rules are processed in order, lower number ids are processed first, so the lowest sequence-id wins. sequence-id is a uint16; if it is not provided it is set to the currently used latest id plus 1, putting the entry at the end of the list, and it can be changed over the lifetime of the access-rule-list to re-sort entries. Bind a list to groups with the user-group leaf-list: add access-rule-list-<name> [user-group <value>] [sequence-id <value>] [description <value>], for example add access-rule-list-A user-group XY. The user-group default is '*', a match-all meaning the list applies to all existing user-groups, and a maximum of 20 user-groups can be referenced. description is a string of 0..256 characters.

Despite the name, auth-key is entirely OSPF-scoped: it holds the pre-shared key for OSPFv3 IPsec integrity protection. The AID is auth-key-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<ospf-if-name>/<spi>, where instance-id is the OSPF instance ID (number, range 0..255), ospf-area-id is the OSPF Router Area ID, ospf-if-name is the reference of the interface in the OSPF area, and spi is a unique security parameter index for this SA (number, range 256..4294967295). Attributes are key, the pre-shared key, a string of length 8..128, and type, which indicates whether the integrity key is ascii or hex encoded. Example: add auth-key-1/0.0.0.0/DCN/256 key abcdefgh12345678. Use set, show and delete on the same key.

Run set authorization mode rules-only. The mode attribute selects which authorization rules are used: static-only (only system defined static rules), static+rules (the default; the system looks for a user configured access-rule first and falls back to system rules) and rules-only (only user defined access-rules; if no rule matches, the global defaults read-default, write-default and exec-default apply). Those three defaults are only configurable when mode = rules-only, each takes permit or deny, and their factory values are read-default permit, write-default deny and exec-default permit, so set read-default deny and exec-default deny to deny anything the rules do not cover. show authorization also reports denied-operations, denied-data-writes and denied-notifications.

A user changes their own password with the password command in Operational mode: password [old-password=<old-password>] [new-password=<new-password>]. Both the old and the new password are required and this is supported only for local users; a password may contain up to 200 characters. Run password with no parameters for interactive input, which prompts for the old password and then the new one twice for confirmation without echoing it (Ctrl+C cancels), or pass them inline for scripts and automation, for example password old-password=Infinera4u! new-password=Infinera4us!. Inline, the standard string rules apply: escape the quote characters with a backslash and enclose #?|; in single or double quotes. To reset another user's password, an administrator uses set user-<username> force-password-change true.

show security displays the top level security container. It takes no parameters and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For the security policy flags underneath it use show security-policies [secure-mode] [strict-password-check] [minimum-password-length] [ssh-authentication-method] [default-user-group] [enforce-password-history-check] [password-history-size] [aaa-authentication-method] [aaa-authorization-method] and the remaining SSH/TLS attributes.

Both are security-policies attributes. minimum-password-length is the configurable minimum length for user passwords, a number in range 1..200 with a default of 8; the length is verified against this policy whenever a password is changed. For history, enforce-password-history-check (true/false, default true) ensures a new password cannot match any of the previous 5 passwords for the user, and password-history-size sets the number of passwords stored for password reuse checking, a number in range 1..200 with a default of 5. strict-password-check (true/false, default true) additionally enforces a minimum of 8 characters plus at least one lower case letter, one upper case letter, one number and one symbol, and forbids the user name inside the password; disabled leaves only a 1 character minimum. These policies only affect newly defined passwords.

The thresholds are per user, on the user object. max-invalid-login is the maximum number of consecutive and invalid login attempts before an account is suspended (locked out): a number in range 0-255, default 5. suspension-time is the duration of UID suspension following those consecutive invalid login attempts, in minutes, range 0-1440, default 5. So by default 5 failed logins lock the account for 5 minutes. Set them with set user-<user-name> max-invalid-login <value> suspension-time <value>. show user-<user-name> reports user-status, which reads lockout when the account is locked out due to unsuccessful login attempts, and failed-logins, the number of previous failed logins, which resets to zero upon a successful login. Lockout can also be turned off globally with the security-policies disable-user-lockout attribute.

show user-data shows the user-data. That is the whole command: it has no parameters and no flags, and is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. If you need per-user detail, use show user-<user-name> instead, which returns password-hashed, user-group, display-name, max-invalid-login, suspension-time, timeout, password-aging-interval, password-expiration-date, enabled, user-status, force-password-change, max-sessions, last-login-date, failed-logins, user-aaa-type, alarm-report-control and label.

Create it with add user-group-<name> [description <value>], in Operational mode or Candidate Configuration mode. The name is a String of 1...64 characters; description is a long description of the user group, a String of 1...128 characters. Each user is associated with a list of groups and derives its permissions from them, so attach it with set user-<user-name> user-group <value>. Manage it with set user-group-<name> description <value>, show user-group-<name> [description] and delete user-group-<name>. Example: add user-group-XY. The predefined groups are EA (Encryption Administrator), MA (Monitoring Access), NA (Network Administrator), NE (Network Engineer), PR (Provisioning), SA (Security Administrator) and TT (Turn-up and Test).

Add/Drop Groups are created with 'add adg-<adg-number>'; adg-number is an integer in the range [1..110], matching the max-adgs value of 110 reported by 'show oadm-capabilities'. Duplication is governed by the read-only wavelength-duplication attribute (show only): 'one-per-adg' (the default) means no duplication of frequencies in the ADG, and 'one-per-degree' means a CDC allows duplication of frequencies in the ADG but only one instance at the Degree. Only CDCs allow more than one instance of the same wavelength on the ADG. Other show attributes are label (String 0..256), max-add-drop-ports (max ports available for the ADG) and bands-supported (not-applicable, standardC-band, superC-band, standardL-band, standardC-standardL-band; default standardC-band). Access mode is Operational or Candidate Configuration.

On 'set amplifier-<name>', gain-target is 0..40 dB with default 0.0 and applies only in manual control mode (control-mode = manual; the alternative and default is auto-max-pw, the auto mode targeting maximum output power). In auto mode you instead use gain-adjustment, an offset in the range [-20.00..20.00] with default 0, supported only on amplifiers whose function is 'pa' or 'inline'. Tilt is not necessarily automatic: tilt-control-mode is manual, auto (default) or auto-planned; auto has the system control tilt from configured fiber parameters and auto-planned from planning-tool parameters. tilt-target [-5..5] dB, default 0dB, applies to manual mode and changing it raises the warning that the attribute may be traffic affecting; tilt-adjustment [-5..5] dB, default 0dB, offsets the target when tilt is auto or auto-planned. When amplifier function is 'add' or 'drop' the only tilt option is manual. gain-operating and tilt-actual are read-only.

Use 'set amplifier-raman-<name> target-raman-gain <value>'. The permitted range is [0, 5..30dB] with default 0dB. It is configurable only when control-mode is different from auto, i.e. auto-planned (user configures target Raman gain plus span attributes) or manual; when control-mode is auto the parameter is ignored and the gain is controlled automatically from the span attributes. Pump count is read from 'show amplifier-raman-<name> number-of-pumps': the value is 4 or 2 for the required-equipped card, and it dictates the number of pump-power objects the system exposes. Related read-only values are total-pump-power (range [-99..99 dBm], -99dBm means no power, the pump power actually sent on port 401 upstream), actual-raman-signal-gain and actual-raman-osc-gain (both 0 when the Raman amplifier is disabled).

Set the ase-idler-enable attribute, either at creation ('add ase-idler-service-<name> [ase-idler-enable <value>]') or afterwards, e.g. 'set ase-idler-service-1-8 ase-idler-enable enabled'. Values are enabled and disabled; the default is disabled. Enabled means ASE idler signal filling on the unused and nmc-failed portions of the band spectrum is turned on. To see whether it actually came up, read the read-only ase-idler-state with 'show ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-state': ase-enabled (filling complete on the band spectrum), ase-partially-enabled (filling incomplete), ase-faulted (ASE idler signal faulted) or ase-disabled (default; signal completely removed). oper-state, avail-state and function (idler) are also available on show. Access mode is Operational or Candidate Configuration.

Use 'set ase-idler-source-<name> target-output-power <value>'. The range is (-3.00..20.50) dBm and the default is 13; it is the ASE pump output power required when manually configured. The pump is not on by default: pump-enable has values enabled and disabled with default disabled, so you must enable it explicitly. The actual pump status is the read-only pump-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled). Example from the guide: 'set ase-idler-source-1-3.1-ase pump-enable 'enabled' target-output-power '15.00''. Other settable attributes are admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), label (0..256) and alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed). function is fixed at ase-idler-source.

Use the calibrate command: 'calibrate [type=]<value> [trigger=]<value> [entity=]<value>'. type must be 'raman' (triggers calibration on raman cards), trigger is 'start' to start the Raman gain calibration for the OTS span or 'stop' to stop it, and entity is the instance to calibrate, which for raman calibration may be an OTS-R entity. Examples: 'calibrate raman start ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line' and 'calibrate raman stop ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line'. The command is available in Operational Mode only. Progress is read with 'show raman-calibration-<name> calibration-state', whose values are not-available (default, never triggered), in-progress, up-to-date, out-dated (for example after OTS OLOS or a delta-pointloss change) and fail; additional-info and gain-calibration-error help troubleshoot fail or out-dated states.

Degrees are created with 'add degree-<degree-number>' where degree-number is an integer in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees; 'show oadm-capabilities max-degrees' reports 20. Grid granularity is reported by the read-only degree attributes: slot-width-granularity, the width of a slot in MHz, default 6250 (6.25 GHz), and center-freq-granularity, the granularity of allowed center frequencies in MHz, default 3125 (3.125 GHz), computed from the base frequency 193.1 THz per G.694.1. Media channels are built from slots: min-slots (default 8) is the minimum number of slots joined to form a media channel and max-slots (default 32) the maximum, with min-slots less than or equal to max-slots. Also shown are is-foadm, wss-less and bands-supported (default standardC-band).

Because the system assigns direction n and direction n+1 automatically to the DWDM Line1 and DWDM Line2 ports of the #n C2ILASGH/D2ILASGM card created, where n is an odd integer with a value between 1 and 15. DWDM Line1 is always assigned an odd index value and DWDM Line2 always an even index value. Accordingly, the read-only direction-number is 1 when direction-port is dwdm-line1 and 2 when it is dwdm-line2. The direction index range is [1..16] (1 and 2 are used when migrating from R6.x). direction-port takes port-<shelf>-<slot>-dwdm-line1 or port-<shelf>-<slot>-dwdm-line2, and the same dwdm-line* port instance of an ILAx can only be selected once per NE. Syntax: 'add direction-<index> direction-port <value> [label <value>]'; 'delete [-f] direction-<index>' forces deletion without confirmation.

On a dsc facility you can configure only label (String 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited; default allowed), using 'add dsc-<name>' or 'set dsc-<name>'. Everything else is show-only: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and managed-by. The managed-by attribute describes whether the facility was system created or not; its values are system and user, with default system, and only user-created facilities can be user deleted. So a dsc showing managed-by system cannot be removed with 'delete dsc-<name>'. Access mode is Operational or Candidate Configuration.

On 'add dsc-group-<name>' or 'set dsc-group-<name>' the pre-FEC threshold is pre-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold, which raises the PRE-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE alarm; it is decimal64 with 3 fraction digits in the range 0|5.600..9.600 dB, where 0 disables threshold crossing alarming, and the specific sub-range depends on the carrier use case. Its hysteresis, pre-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis, is 0.1..1.0 dB with default 0.5. The post-FEC threshold is post-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold, raising POST-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE, range 12.5..18.0 dB with default 18, and post-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis is 0.1..1.0 dB with default 0.5. A related alarm threshold on the same command is dgd-high-threshold for DGD-OORH, uint16 in the range 25..400 ps with default 100. Mandatory creation parameters are carriers and rate.

Use the gadt command, which retrieves information about golden carrier application information from the Golden Application Description Table. The syntax is 'show gadt [<application-description-H|application-description-P|application-description-S|application-description-U>]', so there are four application IDs (H, P, S and U), each a string giving the detailed description of that application ID. For example, 'show gadt application-description-H' returns application-description 'Subsea modes using Uniform and Hybrid modulation'. The application ID also appears as the 'application' field of a golden carrier mode (for instance the P in golden-carrier-mode-800M.95P). Access mode is Operational or Candidate Configuration.

The gapt command lists the golden advanced parameters from the Golden Advanced Parameters Table (GAPT). It is scoped per card type: the syntax is 'show gapt-<card-type> [version] [applicable-resource-type]', where card-type is the card type name, version is the table version (string, length 0..5) and applicable-resource-type is the managed resource type or types applicable for that particular advanced parameter. Plain 'show gapt' lists the tables per card type with their versions, for example gapt-CHM6 at version 1.8, gapt-CHM7 at 3.0 and gapt-CHM7T. 'show gapt-chm7' then lists the individual entries, such as golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/BOASetting, /NLC, /RxCDMode and /TxSignalBWControl, together with the table version. Access mode is Operational or Candidate Configuration.

Use the gcmt command, which retrieves information about the golden carrier mode: 'show gcmt [<card-type>] [version]'. To look up one mode, name it, for example 'show gcmt golden-carrier-mode-800M.95P'. The output lists the golden-carrier-mode (shown fully qualified as golden-carrier-mode-CHM6/800M.95P) with capacity (Gbps) 800, client-mode ethernet-otn, baud-rate (GBaud) 95.2965203, application P, compatibility-id 6 and status supported. For the full per-attribute view use 'show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode>', which adds actual-carrier-mode, sop-tracking-mode, supported-subtypes and candidate-subtypes. Access mode is Operational or Candidate Configuration.

Read the status attribute with 'show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode> status'; it describes the carrier mode release status and its values are supported, candidate, experimental, deprecated and diagnostic. So a mode reporting 'supported' is fully supported, while 'experimental' (or 'candidate' / 'diagnostic') is not. The same status column is returned by 'show gcmt <carrier-mode>'. Per-subtype status is separated out: supported-subtypes lists the subtypes each carrier mode supports (string 0..32, maximum 20 elements) while candidate-subtypes lists the subtypes for which this carrier mode has candidate status (string 0..16, maximum 10 elements). Other attributes on the same command are capacity, client-mode (ethernet or ethernet-otn), baud-rate, application, compatibility-id and sop-tracking-mode.

Use 'show l0-capabilities'. This command shows the capabilities details related with the node's Layer 0 functions. It takes no command parameters, and its access mode is Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode. For the photonic topology limits specifically, the companion command is 'show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs]', which reports the maximum number of degrees (20) and the maximum number of add/drop groups (110).

A Media Channel is created with 'add mc-<name> parent-oms <value> lower-frequency <value> upper-frequency <value> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [auto-delete <value>]'. The three mandatory arguments are parent-oms, lower-frequency and upper-frequency. parent-oms is an instance-identifier set only upon MC creation, and its referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree (it cannot be in an ADG). lower-frequency and upper-frequency are values in MHz. The system derives center-frequency and slot-width (upper-frequency minus lower-frequency) itself, both show-only. auto-delete (disabled by default) lets the system delete the MC when its NMC is deleted; it is allowed only on RD66TM sleds with l0-mode-op=hsc-ols, and is always disabled if l0-mode-op is standard or slte. Example: 'add mc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 parent-oms '1-3.1-dwdm-line' lower-frequency '192225000' upper-frequency '192300000''.

The Media Channel Filler is read only. The mc-f command supports show only: 'show mc-f-<name> [supporting-facilities] [supported-facilities] [supporting-card] [supporting-port] [AID] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [slot-width]'. There is no add, set or delete form. lower-frequency and upper-frequency are the lower and upper frequencies of the MC Filler in MHz, and slot-width is calculated by the system as upper-frequency minus lower-frequency, also in MHz. Access mode is Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode. Note that the sibling nmc-f (Network Media Channel Filler) does accept a limited 'set', for admin-state and alarm-report-control only.

Up to four cards: 'add modules-adg-<adg-number>/<index> supported-card <value> [ocm-monitoring <value>]', where adg-number is in the range [1..110] and index is a number in the range [1..4]. The card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is the card instance identifier. Channel monitoring is on by default: ocm-monitoring has values true and false with default true. It is set upon creation and cannot be changed after supported-card has been assigned; it may optionally be configured to false for OMD cards directly connected to PAx, BAX or C2ILASGH degrees, for example FOADM nodes. Access is Network Administrator or Network Engineer, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. Example: 'add modules-adg-1/1 supported-card card-1-6'.

Use 'add modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>', for example 'add modules-degree-1/1 supported-card card-1-1'. degree-number is a number in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees. The index is 1 only: the card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is the instance identifier of the card or subcard that belongs to the degree, and in R6.0 the card must be RD09SM or RD20TM. You can later change it with 'set modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> [supported-card <value>]', inspect it with the show form, or remove the association with the delete form. Required privilege is Network Administrator or Network Engineer, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode.

Use 'show monitored-channel-<name>/<frequency> monitored-optical-power'. The name corresponds to the WS04S card name with the suffix -1 or -2, for ocm1-in or ocm2-in respectively, and frequency is the nominal center frequency of the carrier in MHz (uint32). monitored-optical-power is the measured power for that carrier in dBm, decimal64 in the range (-99.00..99.00) with default -99, where -99.00 means no power. The other attribute available is monitored-width, the carrier width configured at the NMC within the oxcon source or destination, in MHz (uint32, default 0). Example: 'show monitored-channel-1-1.2-ocm1-in/195987500 monitored-optical-power', or omit the attribute to see both. Access mode is Operational or Candidate Configuration.

On 'add nmc-<name>', center-frequency is the nominal center frequency of the NMC and takes values in the range [190650000..196700000] MHz; it is mandatory at creation along with parent-facility. width is the Network Media Channel frequency width in MHz, with values in the range [15000..200000] MHz and a default of 35000 (35 GHz). The user must configure the 3 dB signal bandwidth, and the value in GHz must be equivalent to the baud rate in GBd configured on the connected transponder line interface line port. Both center-frequency and width are set at creation only (add and show, not set). parent-facility can be a Media Channel or an OMS, is set only upon creation, and its supporting-card must be part of a Degree, not an ADG. Example: 'add nmc-cdc-1-4_192800000-34000 center-frequency 192800000 width 34000 parent-facility oms-1-4-ad1'.

The Network Media Channel Filler occupies 75000 MHz (75 GHz) by default: alloc-bandwidth, the allocated bandwidth of the NMC Filler, is a value in MHz with default 75000. The companion alloc-lower-frequency and alloc-upper-frequency give the allocated bounds, while actual-lower-frequency, actual-upper-frequency and actual-bandwidth give what is actually in place (actual-bandwidth defaults to 0). It is monitored: monitoring-state indicates whether the NMC is intended to be in use, and because this is a system created attribute it is enabled by default (values enabled and disabled, default enabled). Only admin-state and alarm-report-control can be set on nmc-f; power-actual-tx and power-actual-rx are read-only in the range [-99.00..99.00] dBm with default -99.

Use 'show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs]'. max-degrees is the maximum number of degrees, reported as 20 (uint8), and max-adgs is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups, reported as 110 (uint8); either is 0 if not supported. Degrees and ADGs are only supported in OADM node types, and the maximum degrees for the ILA node-type is 0 by convention because an ILA has only 2 directions, fixedly; that case is not shown in supported capabilities. Note that the maximum number of Degrees is not necessarily the deployment supported configuration, but the maximum value of a working degree-number. Sample output: max-degrees 20, max-adgs 110. Access mode is Operational or Candidate Configuration.

On 'set oc-<name>', loopback is the loopback mode, useful to debug on the fiber connection, with values facility, terminal and none, defaulting to none; loopback-mode indicates the loopback action for facility or terminal (values facility, terminal). For test patterns, test-signal-type is the type of test pattern injected, with values none, enumeration, PRBS31Q, PRBS13Q, scrambled-idles, PRBS9 and PRBS31, defaulting to none. test-signal-direction is ingress (the only value, and the default), and test-signal-monitoring turns on monitoring of the incoming test signals for diagnostics, true or false with default false. Example: 'set oc-1-5-T9.1 test-signal-monitoring false'. Related settable attributes include admin-state (lock, maintenance, unlock), tim-monitor, tti-style, tx-tti and expected-tti.

In ILA nodes the OCHm represents the signaled optical channel from the OSC, detected at the ILA OMS by using the OSC information. Consequently, when either the OMS monitoring-mode is 'not-monitored' as configured by the user, or there is no OSC messaging information, the list of OCHm facilities in the NE will be empty. Inspect it with 'show ochm-<name>'; you can set only label, admin-state and alarm-report-control. Read-only values include direction (ingress or egress, only egress is currently supported, default egress) and power-actual, the currently received power in dBm, where -99dBm means the power has not yet been measured by the OCM at the DGE2 card or no power was detected. target-actual-power (-99.00..99.00 dBm) and attenuation-actual (0..55dB) apply to HSC OLS nodes.

Use the ocm-channel facility. It lists the detected carriers within the configured OXcon(s). The command is show only (no add/set/delete), and the key is name plus the slice boundaries: show ocm-channel-<name>/<lower-frequency>/<upper-frequency> [opm-pwr] [connected]. name is a String of length 0..64; lower-frequency and upper-frequency are uint32 and give the lower and upper frequency of the corresponding spectrum power (OPM-pwr point). opm-pwr is the Optical Parameter Monitor power in dBm, decimal64 in the range -99.00..99.00 with default -99. connected yields true if the channel is configured, that is, involved in an oxcon; values are true/false with default false. Access Mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Yes. On the ocm-mp (monitoring point) facility the attribute ocm-enable enables regular power monitoring, takes the values enabled or disabled, and its default is enabled. You set it with: set ocm-mp-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [ocm-enable <value>], and read it with show ocm-mp-<name> ocm-enable. Related read-only attributes: monitored-port (the port being monitored, which can differ from supporting-port for a non-integrated OCM; default not-applicable), ad-direction (reference to the AD coupler/splitter DWDM port, value ingress), and monitoring-state, which the system reports as enabled when an OMS reference exists. admin-state defaults to unlock and managed-by is system. Note that on ocm-ptp the same ocm-enable attribute defaults to disabled instead.

The ocm-ptp facility is available for WS04S cards within a CD-AD ADG and provides dedicated OCM monitoring. It is not enabled out of the box: ocm-enable (enabled/disabled) defaults to disabled, so you must turn it on, for example: set ocm-ptp-1-1.2-ocm1-in ocm-enable enabled. Configurable attributes are label, admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock) and ocm-enable. Read-only attributes include ad-direction (egress or ingress, default ingress), last-measurement (last OCM scan date and time, default never), adg-number (uint8, range 0..110, default 0) and monitoring-state, which the system reports as enabled only when complete connectivity at the AD is established and OCM measurement is possible; its default is disabled.

On the oms facility, grid-mode indicates the grid type of the OMS layer and defaults to flexible, which lets you create and delete MCs of different widths. The other choices are fixed-50G-96ch, fixed-100G-48ch, fixed-75G-64ch, fixed-75G-64ch-oif, fixed-50G-7100 (50 GHz, 88 channels, set automatically when osc-compatibility is osc-7100) and fixed-150G-40ch. Default lower-frequency is 191300000 and upper-frequency 196150000 (standardC-band). monitoring-mode selects how the section is monitored: not-monitored (non-intrusive, no OCM/DGE needed), intrusive (TTP), non-intrusive (CTP, operates with OCM such as DGE), dge-fixed-attenuation, ila-with-equalization (operates with DGE and OCM) and integrated-equalization. Default is intrusive for all node types except ILA, not-monitored for ILA, and integrated-equalization for hyperscale ILA nodes. It is only exposed for an OMS of a port belonging to a degree, or on node-type ILA.

On the Optical Physical Section you can set: label, admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed), input-psd-profile, role and port-expansion. input-psd-profile is the nominal expected tributary channel power density in dBm/12.5GHz, decimal64 in the range -30..-6, default -6. role can be tributary (a single add/drop to a local or remote transponder), multi-carrier (multiple carriers on the underlying filter port), general-purpose (other cases such as express cross-connection to another filter), ase-input (only on specific RD ports in SLTE l0-mode-op) or active-multi-carrier (multiple carriers with active port control); the default is general-purpose. The read-only supported-roles shows which of those the card, and sometimes card-mode, actually allows. port-expansion is no or y-cable, default no, intended for Y-cable expansion. Example: set ops-1-6-ad1 role tributary.

On optical-carrier, frequency is the center frequency the carrier is tuned to, with the overall range 0 | 191275000..196125000 MHz (0 means not configured); the usable sub-range and step depend on module and pluggable, for example CHM7/CHM7X 190625000-196725000 MHz in 50 MHz steps, CHM6 191333000-196117000 MHz, CHM2TX 191292500-196137500 MHz in 1 MHz steps, and CHM1R with TOM-400G-C-DWDM 191275000-196125000 MHz with fine tune. tx-power is the transmit power into the fiber, range -55.0..55.00 dBm with per-module limits (CHM7/CHM7X -10 to 0, default -2; CHM2TX -6 to 0, default 0; UTM2 default -6.0); accuracy is adjustable in 0.5 dBm steps. Yes, you can trim it: frequency-offset gives bright tuning, int16 range -6000..6000 MHz, default 0, and once set the frequency changes slowly over 1-10 s without affecting service.

Yes, use propagate-shutdown on the optical-carrier facility. When set, the transmit laser is shut down if the whole service in that direction has signal failure; it is mainly used at a regeneration node to propagate signal failure as LOS. Values are enabled and disabled, with default disabled. Pair it with propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer, the hold-off time of propagate shutdown, a number in the range 0..2000 milliseconds with default 0. Both are set on the same command: set optical-carrier-<name> [propagate-shutdown <value>] [propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer <value>]. Restriction: neither parameter is configurable on the SPN2 or SPN2C card.

The optical-channel object has a deliberately small configuration surface: the only settable attributes are label (String, length 0..256) and admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock). The syntax is set optical-channel-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>], for example set optical-channel-channel1 admin-state unlock. Everything else is read-only via show optical-channel-<name>: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and managed-by (system or user; only user-created facilities can be user deleted, and the default here is system). Access Mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Read laser-state on the optical-ptp facility: show optical-ptp-<name> laser-state. It reports the emitting pump (for example booster) laser state as enabled or disabled, default disabled; for RD amplifiers it means the source (Tx) pump, for Raman modules the pump laser, and it is only of relevance for DWDM line ports. Yes, you can declare fixed pad: fix-rx-attenuation is the fixed attenuator before port Rx, decimal64 with 2 fraction digits in the range 0..30 dB, default 0, where 0 dB means no fixed attenuator. Example: set -f optical-ptp-1-6-dwdm fix-rx-attenuation 10. There is a matching fix-tx-attenuation (fixed attenuator after port Tx, 0..30 dB, default 0) which is only visible when ops.port-expansion=y-cable is configured. Actual powers are shown by power-actual-rx and power-actual-tx (-99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99 dBm).

The Signal Fail (LOS) decision uses working-los-threshold and protection-los-threshold on the optical-switch facility. Both are configurable optical power in the range -55.0 to 0 dBm and both default to -23 dBm. There is also facility-los-threshold, the threshold of the facility port below which loss of signal is declared, in the range -55 to 15 dBm with default -30.0 dBm. Set them with: set optical-switch-<name> [working-los-threshold <value>] [protection-los-threshold <value>] [facility-los-threshold <value>]. Signal Degrade uses separate thresholds: working-switch-threshold and protection-switch-threshold, -55.0 to 0 dBm, default -18 dBm, and they only trigger switching when switch-threshold-enable is enabled (default disabled). Hysteresis: los-threshold-hysteresis (SF) 0.5 to 5.0 dB in 0.1 dB steps, default 3 dB, and switch-threshold-hysteresis (SD) same range, default 2 dB; 1 dB is recommended for MCHP and OMSP deployments.

On the Optical Supervisory Channel you can set: label, admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed), l0-comm-interface-type, osc-control, target-output-power, tx-power-adjustment, voa-attenuation-target-rx and lof-soak-timer. l0-comm-interface-type selects the SCN IP interface, ipv4 or ipv6; default ipv4 for standard OLS and ipv6 for SLTE and HSC OLS. osc-control is auto or manual, default auto; auto has been supported since R6.0.1 and HSC OLS nodes only support auto. target-output-power is the OSC Tx power at the DWDM line port output, na or -2.5..4.5 dBm, default na. tx-power-adjustment trims the automatically calculated Tx target, na or -6..6 dB, default 0. voa-attenuation-target-rx is the Rx VOA target for manual mode, 0..30 dB, default 10. lof-soak-timer is short (about 3 ms) or long (adds 18,400 OC-3 frames, about 2300 ms), default short, and is only visible for the PBAx card.

Read otdr-state on the otdr facility: show otdr-<name> otdr-state. Its values are not-available (status is not available), idle, measuring (measurement is ongoing), finished (measurement has completed) and fail (measurement has failed); the default is not-available, and a status change triggers a change notification. Alongside it, otdr-measurement-time gives the time remaining in the current run (integer, default 0), otdr-error carries the error message produced when a measurement ends with error, otdr-laser-state shows the laser as not-available/enabled/disabled, otdr-measurement-port shows the port being measured (0 means no port is being measured), otdr-measurement-direction shows not-available, tx or rx, and otdr-ongoing-measurement-profile shows which pre-defined profile is running: none, short, medium, long, raman-precheck1, raman-precheck2 or raman-precheck3.

On otdr-ptp you can add or set otdr-range, otdr-pulse-width, otdr-measurement-speed, otdr-ior, otdr-fiber-type, otdr-resolution, otdr-direction-mode, peak-power and launching-fiber-length. otdr-range is the distance range, auto or 0...300.0 km, default auto; set it to the fiber length plus 10 percent (from R9.1 auto is derived from the OTS fiber-length values with 10 percent margin, rounded up to the nearest 10 km). otdr-pulse-width is auto or 10...20,000 ns, default auto. otdr-resolution is the data sampling resolution, auto or 0.4...100.0, default auto. otdr-measurement-speed is fast (about 10 s), medium (about 15 s), slow (about 1 min), precision (3-5 min), high-precision (5-7 min) or auto, default auto. otdr-ior is auto or 1.0...2.0. peak-power is auto or 5...14.5. launching-fiber-length is 0...50 m, default 0, and is deducted from the result; auto is not supported. otdr-direction-mode defaults to counter-prop-in-service.

Declare it on the ots facility. fiber-type-tx and fiber-type-rx name the fibre at the transmitter and receiver; both default to SSMF and accept AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor. fiber-length-tx and fiber-length-rx are auto or 0..500.0 km, default auto, and are needed for tilt control and for Raman backward pumping. Loss is set with span-loss-transmit and span-loss-receive, decimal64 in 0..80 dB (span-loss-receive also allows 99), default 0; this is fibre loss only, and extra loss such as patch panels goes in external-attenuation-tx and external-attenuation-rx (0..30 dB, default 0). Changing span-loss-receive is traffic affecting. span-loss-reference chooses which source power control uses, configured or measured, default measured. The system reports span-loss-derived-rx/tx, fiber-length-derived-rx/tx and span-loss-alarm-threshold.

The ots-diagnostics name is auto generated by the system when the line card is provisioned; you never create it. The format is ots-diagnostics-<chassis>-<slot>-<DWDM Line>, so a diagnostics object on chassis 1, slot 1, DWDM line is shown as show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line, and a C2ILASGH with two lines gives ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line1 and ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line2. On that object only two attributes are settable: nmoper-alarm-reporting (disabled/enabled, default disabled), which when enabled raises the NMOPER alarm on a mismatch between expected-operator and rx-operator, and expected-operator (up to 32 characters, empty by default). tx-operator is read-only and is defaulted by the system to <ne-name>-<Dxx>, that is <ne-name>-D00.

The ots-r facility assumes SSMF: required-fiber-type-rx is the required fibre type on the DWDM line for the Rx fibre and defaults to SSMF, with the choices AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor; it is only of relevance if control-mode = auto and there is no fiber-connection. About the receive span you can also declare fiber-length-rx (unspecified or 0..500.0, default unspecified), span-loss-receive (the span loss at the receiving dwdm-line, default 99), external-attenuation-rx (user configured external attenuation) and delta-pointloss, the additional Rx attenuation determined after turning up pumps, not-applicable or -1..3.5 dB, default not-applicable. Read-only: configured-fiber-type-rx, configured-fiber-length-rx, span-loss-at-amplifier, power-actual-rx and connected-reference. Example: set ots-r-11-2-dwdm-line external-attenuation-rx 2.

Yes, and the default does depend on that. The ots-r-auto-otdr entity on an ots-r container carries automatic-otdr, which enables or disables OTDR based automatic fibre check; values are enabled and disabled, with the default enabled for green field deployments and disabled for in-field SW upgrade. If the Raman card is associated with a base card equipped with integrated OTDR the default value is enabled; if the NE has a Raman card that is not aggregated with the EDFA card the value is disabled. The setting persists over warm and cold restart and over SW upgrade. Disabling it during an active test aborts the ongoing OTDR test and releases the amplifier that automatic OTDR had blocked; disabling it with no test running stops further tests until re-enabled. Progress is read from auto-otdr-state: not-applicable, not-available, pass, in-progress, fail or aborted. Example: set ots-r-auto-otdr-1-1-dwdm-line automatic-otdr enabled.

Create it with add oxcon-<name> source <value> destination <value> [label] [activation-mode] [auto-delete] [activation-request-fwd] [activation-request-bwd] [direction] [target-output-power-src] [target-output-power-dst] [circuit-id], for example add oxcon-1-80-192262500__1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 source 'nmc-1-80-192262500' destination 'nmc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500'. source and destination are the required end-point instance IDs; direction is two-way or one-way, default two-way. Whether it comes up on its own is set by activation-mode, which can only be given at add: automatic means the system activates the service on creation and deactivates it on deletion (standard L0 mode), manual means you drive it with activation-request-fwd/bwd (SLTE mode), and activate-on-create is the HSC OLS mode. The default is automatic for standard mode, manual for SLTE, activate-on-create for HSC OLS. target-output-power-src/dst range -18.00..15.00 dBm.

profile-control applies only to the RD20TM operating in card-mode = slte or slte-backhaul. Syntax: profile-control [type=]<value> [entity=]<value> [direction=]<value> [[profile-data=]<value>], Access Mode is Operational Mode. type is write-attenuation-profile, read-attenuation-profile, create-power-profile, read-power-profile or read-ocm-power (reads OCM data from an OMS entity). direction is tx or rx, but for power-profile only tx is supported. For RD20TM in card-mode = slte the power profile and OCM power are defined at the output of the booster, before the EVOA, not at the DWDM line out port. The OMS attenuation string is <StartFreq>,<SlotWidth>,<AttnValue1>,... with attenuation 0 - 25.50 and N = 776 for standardC-band at 6.25 GHz; the NMC string allows -10 - 25.50 and N no greater than 32. Example: profile-control read-power-profile oms-1-8-dwdm-line tx.

The pump command is nearly all read-only. With set pump-<name> you can change only three things: label (String, length 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance) and alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default Allowed). Everything else is display only through show pump-<name>: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled), avail-state (in-service, out-of-service, normal, abnormal, low-power), managed-by (system or user, where only user-created facilities can be user deleted) and pump-type. Access Mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. To change pump power itself, use the separate pump-power command and its target-pump-power attribute.

Use the pump-power object, keyed by pump name and pump-id, where pump-id is an integer identifying the number of the pump: set pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> [target-pump-power <value>]. target-pump-power is the Raman pump power required in dBm and applies when the control-mode is manual; its range is -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable (default not-applicable), and 0 is the not-applicable case. On an RPBM card the target-pump-power must be in the range 12 to 30 dBm. If the value is outside the operating range of the Raman sled, the PUMP-Fail (STAT FAIL PSTAT) alarm is raised. The allowed limits are read back with show pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> min-target-pump-power max-target-pump-power, both decimal64 with 2 fraction digits in -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable. configured-pump-power shows what is programmed in hardware (derived automatically if control-mode is auto, otherwise from target-pump-power) and actual-pump-power shows the measured value, default -99.

Read calibration-state on the raman-calibration facility: show raman-calibration-<name> calibration-state, for example show raman-calibration-1-8. It reports the state of the automatic Raman gain calibration process as not-available (calibration has not been triggered or no prior calibration occurred), in-progress (currently running), up-to-date (completed successfully and current), out-dated (stale because of OTS OLOS, a change in delta pointloss and similar) or fail (ended with a failure). The default is not-available. Supporting read-only attributes: last-calibration-timestamp (date-and-time or never, default never) tells you when the last calibration rpc completed, gain-calibration-error gives the residual gain error per iteration in dB, calibrated-delta-pointloss gives the suggested delta-pointloss in the range -3..3.5 dB, and intermediate-results and additional-info carry troubleshooting text when the state is fail or out-dated.

rsc is the Raman card Pilot Tone facility. Configuration is limited: set rsc-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>], where admin-state takes Unlock, Locked, Maintenance or Unknown with default Unlocked, and alarm-report-control is Allowed or Inhibited with default Allowed. What it reports is the pilot tone power in both directions: rsc-power-rx, the received Pilot Tone integrated power, and rsc-power-tx, the transmitted Pilot Tone integrated power. show rsc-<name> also returns supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, label, oper-state (enabled/disabled, default enabled), avail-state and managed-by (system or user, default system; only user-created facilities can be user deleted). Access Mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Because the spectrum facility is only instantiated by the system when the underlying server layer OMS has monitoring-mode configured as either non-intrusive or ila-with-equalization. Its existence depends entirely on the OMS monitoring-mode, and the object is only of relevance if the DGE2 is intended to be used in the NE. So check and, if appropriate, change monitoring-mode on the corresponding oms facility. Once it exists, spectrum lets you set label, admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed) and attenuation-setting, a unique attenuation value for the entire spectrum in the range 0..30 dB, default 0 dB, editable only when attenuation-control-mode = manual and control-mode = auto-max-pw. The read-only dge-in-use reports true when the corresponding OMS monitoring-mode is ila-with-equalization.

Use spectrum-control, which is keyed by entity name, direction and band slice center frequency: add|set|delete spectrum-control-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [attenuation-target <value>] [target-output-power <value>], and show spectrum-control-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [width] [attenuation-actual] [attenuation-target] [target-output-power]. direction is ingress or egress with default egress, and currently only egress is supported. center-frequency is in MHz and is managed by the system. attenuation-target is the required attenuation for the spectra, range 0..30 dB, default 0, and it is only possible to configure when a Dynamic Gain Equalizer (dge-in-use = 'true'), or equivalent, is in use. target-output-power is the intended target output power, not-specified or -55..55 dBm, default not-specified. attenuation-actual (read-only, dB) is likewise only readable with a DGE in use, and width returns the detected width in MHz or 0 if no match, or no ILAx card or DGE fiber-connected. Example: set spectrum-control-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/194943750 attenuation-target 1.

Use show spectrum-monitoring-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [width] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [target-actual-power] [power-actual] [psd-actual]. name is a string 0..64; direction is ingress or egress, default egress, and only egress is currently supported; center-frequency is the band slice center frequency in MHz and is managed by the system. width is the received NMC width in MHz, default 50000. lower-frequency and upper-frequency give the media channel edges in MHz. power-actual is the currently received power in dBm, default -99; -99 dBm means the power has not yet been measured by the OCM on the DGE2 card, or no power was detected (or no appropriate fiber connection). For egress, power-actual is calibrated at the DWDM line port output, the same reference point where target power is defined. target-actual-power is the ATPS-calculated target, default -99 dBm, relevant only when target-power-setting = auto. psd-actual is the calculated Power Spectral Density in nW/GHz to 2 digit precision, default not-applicable, and does not depend on spectra width. Example: show spectrum-monitoring-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/191968750. Available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Read the contention-check-status attribute on the super channel. You can pass it on add super-channel-<name> carriers <value> carrier-mode <value> [label] [admin-state] [alarm-report-control] [contention-check-status], and read it with show super-channel-<name> ... [contention-check-status]. It is the Contention Check state set via DNA in openwave mode, with values pending, success, overridden and failk, defaulting to pending. It is only applicable if openwave-contention-check is enabled at the super-channel-group level; that attribute enables the DNA assisted contention control mechanism in openwave mode, takes false or true, and defaults to false. So enable openwave-contention-check on the super-channel-group first, otherwise contention-check-status stays meaningless. Related power context on the super channel: line-system-mode defaults to openwave, and expected-total-tx-power (theoretical total TX power at the faceplate, computed from per-carrier target TX power) defaults to -55.

-m is the merge configuration flag. The add command for super-channel-group works in merge mode only, so -m performs a best effort add: if the target entity does not exist it is created, and if it already exists it is updated with whatever attributes are present on the add command. In other words the command will not fail if the entity already exists. Full syntax: add -m super-channel-group-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <lock|unlock|maintenance>] [auto-in-service-enabled <value>] [valid-signal-time <value>] [alarm-report-control <allowed|inhibited>] [line-system-mode <value>] [openwave-contention-check <value>]. Defaults on that object: admin-state unlock, alarm-report-control allowed, auto-in-service-enabled false, valid-signal-time 480 minutes (range 1..7200), line-system-mode openwave, managed-by user, oper-state disabled. The same -m merge behaviour applies to comm-channel.

Use show supported-carrier-mode-<name>/<carrier-mode> [capacity] [client-mode] [baud-rate] [application] [compatibility-id] [status] [supported-subtypes], which displays the list of supported carrier modes. carrier-mode is an acronymized code (handle) for the optical carrier line mode 4-tuple, formatted <Capacity><ClientMode>.<Baud Rate><Application ID>, string length 1..15, for example 600E.84P, 100X.73U or 325M.66P. capacity is the net capacity of the optical carrier in gbps, so that attribute answers the capacity question per mode. client-mode is the digital client mode mapped into and transported by the carriers in the superchannel, either ethernet or ethernet-otn. baud-rate is the modulated symbol rate. application is the optical transport application ID the mode is optimized for, string length 1..15. compatibility-id identifies which carrier modes can be applied simultaneously. status is the state of the carrier mode. supported-subtypes lists subtypes each carrier mode supports, string 0..32 with a maximum of 20 elements. Access: Operational mode and Candidate configuration mode.

Use show supported-gain-range-<name>/<gain-range-type> [gain-range-min] [gain-range-max]. gain-range-type takes low, high or standard. gain-range-min is the minimum settable gain-target for that type of range (standard, low or high) and gain-range-max is the maximum settable gain-target for that range; both are of type gain-value with no default. So the numeric limits behind the low, standard and high settings are not fixed constants in the command definition, they are reported per entity by these two read-only attributes. The command is display only, available in Operational mode and Candidate configuration mode.

A card type can expose several power profiles because different profiles reflect different scenarios when using that card. The user defines, per card instance, which profile is in effect, and that choice has an impact on the power estimation for the system. Inspect them with show supported-power-profile-<card-type>/<name> [profile-description] [power-draw] [default]. card-type is the card type string and name is the profile name. profile-description is a string 0..255 describing the profile. power-draw is a decimal64 giving the power draw of the associated equipment when not in low-power. default is true or false, indicating whether that profile is the default value. Access: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

It depends on router-id-mode. Syntax: add bgp-instance-<instance-id> local-as <value> [description <value>] [router-id-mode <value>] [router-id <value>], and the same optional attributes are settable with set bgp-instance-<instance-id>. router-id-mode takes use-loopback or manual and defaults to use-loopback, meaning by default the router ID is taken from the loopback IP. Set router-id-mode manual and supply router-id to specify it yourself. router-id accepts an IPv4 or IPv6 address, but 0.0.0.0/0 is not supported for IPv4 and 0::0.0 is not supported for IPv6. instance-id is a string 1..255, local-as is mandatory on add and ranges 1..4294967295, description is a string 0..128, and vrf is read only via show. Example: add bgp-instance-10 local-as 24 router-id-mode use-loopback.

Defaults on bgp-neighbor are connect-retry-interval 120 seconds (range 1..65535), hold-time 90 seconds (range 3..65535), and keepalive-interval 30 seconds (range 1..21845). The guide notes hold-time is typically 3x the keepalive-interval and keepalive-interval is typically 1/3 the hold-time. negotiated-hold-time is a show-only value, 0..65535 seconds, default 0. Yes, you can authenticate the session: secure-session sets the authentication method to none or TCP-MD5, default none, and password carries the TCP-MD5 authentication key in ASCII, string 0..80. Syntax: add bgp-neighbor-<instance-id>/<remote-address> peer-as <value> [afi-safis] [enabled] [description] [secure-session] [password] [connect-retry-interval] [hold-time] [keepalive-interval]; all of those except peer-as and afi-safis are also changeable with set. enabled defaults to true; setting it false ceases an ESTABLISHED session and blocks both outgoing and incoming TCP attempts.

The route has to be in the forwarding table already. The guide states that routes to be advertised to an external AS must exist in the forwarding table installed by an Interior Gateway Protocol such as OSPF, or by static routes, but not by BGP itself. For routes not present in the IGP tables you must configure blackhole static routes: set the special-next-hop parameter of the static route command to blackhole, for example on ipv4-static-route or ipv6-static-route where special-next-hop takes the value blackhole. Then create the bgp-network object with add bgp-network-<instance id>/<remote-address>/<network prefix>; a maximum of 100 bgp-network MOs can be configured. instance-id is a string 1..255, remote-address is the peer address in IPv4 or IPv6 (0.0.0.0/0 and 0::0.0 are not supported), and network-prefix is a decimal 1..64 or 128. Example: add bgp-network-10/2620:38:4001:192::65/3000::2/64.

mtu on comm-channel is the maximum transmission unit size in octets for the physical Ethernet port of the comm channel, and it is available only when mode is L3 (mode values are L1 ETH User Channel, L2 iGCC interface, L3 IP mode, default L3). It is a uint16 with a platform dependent range: 1280..1500 octets on 1830 GX G30 only, and 1280..9202 octets on 1830 GX G40 only. The default is 1500; for 1830 GX G40 the per interface type defaults are 1518 for DCN, AUX, AUX2, OFEC-CC, Craft, CHM6 and UCM4. Set it with add -m comm-channel-<name> type <value> parent <value> [... mtu <value> ...] or set comm-channel-<name> mtu <value>. Related L3-only attributes: mru 64..1500 octets default 1500, restart-timer 1..10 seconds default 3, max-failure 2..10 default 5, peer-address default 0.0.0.0. Example: add comm-channel-gcc0 type GCC0 label GCC0 alarm-report-control allowed mtu 1500 parent otu-1-6-1-OTUC4.

LLDP is off by default. lldp-admin-status defaults to disabled, meaning the agent neither transmits nor receives LLDP frames; the other values are tx-only, rx-only and tx-and-rx. It cannot be modified if mode is L1. lldp-transmit-interval is 1..16383 seconds, default 30. lldp-mgmt-addr-if selects which interface IP is used as the management address and must be set explicitly by the user; it applies when lldp-admin-status is tx-only or tx-and-rx, and takes 1-AUX-1, 1-AUX-2, DCN, DCN-2 (G30 only), 1-AUX-1-B, 1-AUX-2-B, DCN-B, DCN-2-B (G30 only) or L0-MGMT. It is empty by default, in which case the system uses the loopback IP if configured, otherwise the DCN/AUX IP, and sends no TLV if neither has an address. Auto-negotiation is on: auto-negotiation defaults to enabled. rate (1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000 Mbits or maximum) defaults to maximum, duplex-mode defaults to full, and flow-control defaults to disabled, but all three are only valid when auto-negotiation is disabled. Example: set comm-eth-1-5-ETH1 lldp-admin-status tx-and-rx.
